=== B2 (BLOCKING). The PR body's account of WHY lwb-lanes fails is wrong at this head, and the true cause is an identifier this branch introduces. ===
The body says the failure is pre-existing and not this branch's content: "reviews/35/cloud-reviewer.json is STALE and reviews/35/cloud-reviewer-b.json's AGREE is rejected on a same-repo-name segment collision ... Neither record lives under reviews/37/."
That is not what the gate says now. Running the gate as CI runs it:
    python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base <live main> --head HEAD --pr-number 38 -> exit 1
    FAIL: reviews/38/cloud-reviewer.json:   reviewer_id and commit_author_id share the
          segment 'buildcraft' (10 characters, at or above MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8)
    FAIL: reviews/38/cloud-reviewer-b.json: (the same)
    plus a cascade of 32 per-commit failures, each "touches a shared path and has 0
    independent review(s) in reviews/38/".
The records are under reviews/38/, not reviews/35/, and the segment they collide on is 'buildcraft' -- the repository's own name.
PROVED BY PROBE, working-tree only, restored afterwards, nothing committed:
    P1  remove the repo-name segment from reviews/38/cloud-reviewer.json's reviewer_id alone
        -> the entire 32-commit cascade DISAPPEARS; the only line left is the other
           record still colliding. exit 1.
    P2  remove it from BOTH reviewer ids
        -> "lwb-lanes check passed", exit 0.
P1 is the control that the probe is not vacuous and localises the cause to exactly one thing. P2 establishes that the shared repository-name segment is the SOLE blocker on this pull request. Tree restored; `git status --porcelain` empty.
ATTRIBUTION, traced rather than asserted. I read every review record on main: not one merged author id carries a 'buildcraft' segment (#27's is claude-lwb-agent-leapware-hq-..., and 7-26 use coordinator-opus5-... or claude-code-opus5-...). The reviewer-side convention carrying 'buildcraft' is older than this branch. What is new here is proof/38.json's `author` field, "conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19", which the two reviewers copied into commit_author_id. Putting the repository's own name into an author identifier makes it collide with every reviewer identity that also names the repository, and the repository name carries no identifying information at all -- it is the one segment guaranteed to be shared. This is the false-positive class MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH's own comment anticipates and explicitly declines to resolve ("no value closes both. The trade is recorded here rather than resolved"), now realised against the name of the repository itself.
This is fixable inside this pull request and does not need a gate change: an author identifier that does not embed the repository name restores the gate to green, as P2 shows.

=== AND IT REJECTS ME TOO. I AM NOT RELABELLING TO GET AROUND IT. ===

I did not: there is a decision on the books against relabelling an identifier to make a gate pass, and doing it to file my own record would be the worst possible place to start. I kept the mandated string verbatim, appended this session's real token and today's date, and am reporting the collision instead. Treat this record as evidence, not as a key.
